title.narrative: Strengthen the legal identity and civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) ecosystem in Samoa, leveraging digitalization

description.narrative: The development challenge this project aims to address is the inefficiency and incompleteness of Samoa’s Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) data system, which is a critical statistical record of vital events fundamental for individuals and governments. The current system faces delays in notification and registration of CRVS vital events, particularly those from rural, remote areas, and underserved communities. Most of the CRVS records and historical data are still in paper formats, which are vulnerable to damage or destruction during natural disasters like cyclones or tsunamis. Data silos and data fragmentation of CRVS records hinder interoperability and data sharing. This impacts the data information needed for effective planning, policymaking, public health monitoring, and the delivery of essential services. It also impacts individuals ability to access social services and legal recognition, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized groups such as women and children, particularly from rural, remote areas.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
